one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent successfully navigated environment setup issues and prepared training data, but the fastText training call timed out under the 120s IPython cell limit due to resource-intensive parameters (epoch=10, minn=3, maxn=6, bucket=1000000) on 650k samples, and the subsequent attempt with reduced parameters crashed the runtime entirely.
t_err_evidence: Step 27 executes fasttext.train_supervised with epoch=10, dim=100, minn=3, maxn=6, bucket=1000000 on 650k training samples inside an IPython cell with a 120s timeout; the cell times out with '[Execution timed out (120.0 seconds).]', confirming the parameters were too resource-intensive for the available execution budget.
t_commit_evidence: After the step-27 timeout, only one step remains (step 28), which is also blocked by a runtime crash; no successful training or model save ever occurs, so the failure is locked in at step 27.
t_surface_evidence: Step 27 produces '[Execution timed out (120.0 seconds).]' — the first observable signal that training cannot complete under the given resource constraints.
trigger_explanation: The IPython cell has a hard 120-second execution timeout, and the container has limited CPU/memory. Training fastText with epoch=10, minn=3, maxn=6, bucket=1000000 on 650,000 samples far exceeds that budget. The agent did not set a longer timeout via the execute_bash timeout parameter, did not use the fastText CLI (which would bypass IPython limits), and did not pre-estimate training time before committing to these parameters. This is a real environment obstacle (resource/timeout limit) that was handled incorrectly.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 4-20 involved repeated stalled fasttext pip wheel builds (each cancelled with Ctrl-C), signaling that build/execution in this environment is slow and resource-constrained. Steps 4, 5, 10, 11 all show the fasttext wheel build hanging, indicating compute limits before any training was attempted.
